cards.explanation: The answer is music. David, Israel's king, put these Levites in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there (1 Chronicles 6:31). A bakery needs a little song too, friends, because nobody gets through a long batch in silence. Mine is mostly humming and a timer that doesn't care.

The answer is the tabernacle. The singers ministered with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6:32). The verse tells us exactly where they sang and how long. I like a clear schedule, friends, and I know a thing or two about being put in a spot and told to get to work.

The answer is that they did it according to the regulations given them. The singers performed their duties "…according to the regulations given them." (1 Chronicles 6:32) So even the music had an order to it. I can respect that, friends, because even my cookies come out better when I follow the recipe instead of my feelings.

The answer is every kind of service of the tabernacle. Their fellow Levites "…were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God." (1 Chronicles 6:48) Every kind! That's a long list, and I bet somebody was always wiping something down. I know that life, friends, because I once had to scrub my own apron.

The answer is False. The text says "…Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place." (1 Chronicles 6:49) The other Levites had plenty to do, since they were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 6:48), but that room's work wasn't theirs. Some jobs have one set of hands, friends, like my cookie stamp.

The answer is to make atonement for Israel. Aaron and his sons presented the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense "…to make atonement for Israel…" (1 Chronicles 6:49) That's the heart of their work, and it's serious business. It points me toward Jesus, the Lamb, who gave His life to rescue people (Mark 10:45).

The answer is True. Aaron and his sons did their work "…according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded." (1 Chronicles 6:49) Moses, Israel's leader, gave the instructions, and they followed them. That's the kind of baking I like, friends, where you read the whole recipe first, which I rarely do.

The answer is that the first lot fell to them. The text says they come first "…because the first lot fell to them…" (1 Chronicles 6:54) So it came down to the lot. Nobody had to argue over who goes first, friends, and I wish deciding who gets the first cookie off the tray were that easy.
